divergences.description: Unconstrained abstract state machines (S1) replace neural networks: both P-D51b (Schäfer & Zimmermann, 2006) and P-H11 (machine-learning/unrolled feedforward networks) concern neural networks with constrained unit state spaces and fixed activation forms, whereas S1 allows every unit n to have an arbitrary type A3 n as its state space (e.g., Option (List X), storing unbounded input histories verbatim) and allows completely arbitrary functions for local updates a5 and global readout a6. This trivializes universality—T units can simply act as an f-independent shift register buffering the input sequence while the unrestricted readout a6 evaluates f directly—establishing something materially different from neural-network universality.

Exact computation replaces universal function approximation: P-D51b states that any input-output function can be approximated to any degree of accuracy (a metric/topological approximation property), whereas Target asserts exact equality N.d4 xs = f xs for arbitrary functions f : List X → Y on arbitrary types X and Y, with no metric, topology, or approximation error.

Finite-horizon weakening: neither P-D51b ('any input-output function') nor P-H11 ('implement any function, even when time plays a role') restricts the claim to a fixed finite horizon (though P-H11 mentions unrolled networks as an example). Target restricts agreement to sequences with xs.length ≤ T, with the network N allowed to depend on T and completely unconstrained on sequences longer than T; this materially weakens the statement because no single finite acyclic S1 system can implement an arbitrary unbounded-horizon function f : List X → Y.

Architecture mismatch with P-D51b: P-D51b states its universal approximation claim specifically for recurrent neural networks (not feedforward networks, contrary to the author's summary), whereas P-H11 makes the claim for feedforward networks. Target requires strict acyclicity (N.D9), matching P-H11 while excluding recurrent systems (N.D10).

Added exact unit-count condition (N.d13 = T): neither source passage claims that exactly T units suffice independently of the complexity of f or the size of X and Y. Target adds this strengthening, which only holds because of the unconstrained unit state types and arbitrary update/readout functions.

Discrete-time synchronous idealization and functional acyclicity: Target models time specifically as discrete finite sequences List X with synchronous updates where every unit receives the external input x at every step and a6 reads all units simultaneously, rather than continuous time or layered network wiring; furthermore, feedforwardness (N.D9) is defined via functional dependence of a5 across all (including unreachable) global states rather than structural graph acyclicity.

judgement.summary: Target is divergent from P-D51b and P-H11 because it replaces neural-network universal approximation and unrestricted temporal implementation with an exact, finite-horizon result for abstract state machines with arbitrary unit state types and arbitrary transition/readout functions. Because any function f can be computed by buffering the last T inputs in arbitrary-type registers and applying f directly in the readout, the formal statement establishes something materially weaker and conceptually different from the neural-network claims in the sources.
